summary:
Storm Watch is an offline-capable, bilingual (English and Afaan Oromo) space weather mission game for ages 7–12 where real NASA solar storm data sets the clock. Instead of reading passive radiation facts, players command a Moon or Mars habitat for seven sols and make high-stakes survival trade-offs.

Real NASA CCMC DONKI flare and particle timestamps drive three core mechanics: the Storm Clock (deciding when to shelter under uncertain warning times and real false alarms), Same Storm, Two Worlds (replaying the exact same storm on the Moon vs. Mars across lower sunlight, dust storms, and 3–22 minute radio delays), and What Would Have Saved You? (a deterministic replay solver proving the smallest fix after any loss). Zero-login and transparently labeled LIVE or SAVED, it brings real NASA data into any classroom.
details:
THE CHALLENGE & WHY IT MATTERS

Space weather decides whether lunar and Martian crews stay safe, yet radiation science often feels abstract to students aged 7–12. Storm Watch turns real solar physics into hands-on command decisions: balancing limited solar power, breathable air, habitat shielding, and scientific discovery while an uncertain solar storm closes in.

WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Players manage a seven-sol mission at Moon (Entoto Base) or Mars (Dallol Base) across two difficulty levels: Cadet (ages 7–9, guided presets, 0.7x radiation) and Commander (ages 10–12, direct bolt allocation, 1.0x radiation). Every sol, crews spend limited power bolts (15 power each) across Air, Shielding, and Science Labs.

On a hidden storm sol, real NASA DONKI flare (FLR) and solar energetic particle (SEP) records—spanning 0.25–48 hour arrival gaps as well as real unlinked false-alarm flares—generate a 1-to-4 block Storm Clock:

1. Predict First: Players forecast whether fast particles will follow the flare, building scientific intuition and a personal Forecaster Score.

2. Beat the Storm Clock: Each block forces a tense choice—Work outside (+1 science, risking full unshielded dose if particles arrive early) or Shelter now (safe behind habitat shielding, sacrificing science if it is a false alarm).

3. Compare Two Worlds: Fly the exact same storm and seed on the Moon, then Mars. Lower Martian sunlight (24 vs. 42 power), a seeded dust storm, and a 3–22 minute Earth-to-Mars radio delay visibly shrink reaction time and shift outcomes in a 5-row debrief comparison.

4. Learn Without Blame: On any run under 3 stars, a deterministic replay engine (findSaver) tests 1- and 2-step plan edits to prove the exact change that would have saved the crew, paired with Curiosity MSL RAD facts and a 3-question comprehension check.

CREATIVITY & HUMAN-CENTERED DESIGN

- Physics-Honest Simplification: Radiation shields strongly reduce solar storm particle damage while steady cosmic rays still chip away daily—and a built-in "What is simplified?" guide transparently distinguishes game mechanics from NASA measurements.

- Cultural & Planetary Context: Outpost names honor Ethiopia's Entoto Observatory and the Dallol Mars-analogue site in Afar, paired with bilingual English and Afaan Oromoo support and high-legibility Atkinson Hyperlegible typography.

- Classroom & Low-Bandwidth Ready: Features a Classroom Mode (silencing audio/vibration + printable 5-group challenge scoreboard), 10-minute Teacher Lab plan, seeded Daily Missions, Storm Collection unlocks, and honest LIVE vs. SAVED data badges so classrooms never stall when offline.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & TECHNICAL FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Frontend & 3D Scene: React 19, TypeScript 5.7, Vite 6, custom SVG illustrations, procedural Three.js 3D outpost (with automatic 2D fallback for low-power/reduced-motion devices), and synthesized Web Audio sound cues.

- Data & Offline Resilience: Serverless proxy (/api/donki) querying NASA CCMC DONKI with caching and an 8-second timeout, backed by a hand-verified offline snapshot and vite-plugin-pwa service worker (<1 MB).

- Quality & Accessibility Verification: Validated with deterministic Vitest unit suites, 5,000-run balance verification, star-reachability proofs, Playwright end-to-end tests across mobile/desktop viewports, and axe-core accessibility audits.
